vocab.source_excerpt: I mean, there are like a lot of branding gone wrong where plaintiffs need skin grafts in extreme cases because they were branded by some sort of hot iron tool.
vocab.tip: Iron is usually pronounced like EYE-ern in American English, not eye-ron. Attach the word to the metal in an iron tool.
vocab.example: The old gate was made of iron.
vocab.example_cn: 这扇旧门是铁制的。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Material in hot iron tool, not the action of smoothing clothes.

vocab.definition: lasting rather than temporary or expected to end soon
vocab.source_excerpt: Now they need new skin or paddling gone wrong, causing permanent aesthetic and emotional damage to one's bottom.
vocab.tip: Pair permanent with temporary as opposites. A permanent mark stays; keep -nent at the end, not -nate.
vocab.example: The leak caused permanent damage to the floor.
vocab.example_cn: 漏水给地板造成了永久性损坏。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Duration of harm described in source; not an independently confirmed prognosis.

vocab.definition: a person or organization bringing a civil court case against another
vocab.source_excerpt: I mean, there are like a lot of branding gone wrong where plaintiffs need skin grafts in extreme cases because they were branded by some sort of hot iron tool.
vocab.tip: Link plaintiff with complaint: the plaintiff brings the complaint to court. Keep double f at the end and contrast with defendant.
vocab.example: The plaintiff filed a complaint against the company.
vocab.example_cn: 原告对这家公司提起了诉讼。
vocab.context_review_note: Claimant role, not necessarily a proven victim or a prosecutor.

vocab.definition: a prospective member undergoing a fraternity's joining process
vocab.cn: 兄弟会准成员；入会新人
vocab.source_excerpt: Also, you could tear your rectum and sustain injuries like this very bright-minded pledge did.
vocab.tip: Pledge can mean a promise; here it names the person beginning membership. Remember new pledge to keep the person sense distinct.
vocab.example: The club welcomed its new pledges.
vocab.example_cn: 该社团欢迎新入会的准成员。
vocab.context_review_note: Person, not a promise or donation; very bright-minded is sarcasm in the source.

vocab.definition: the final part of the large intestine before the anus
vocab.source_excerpt: Also, you could tear your rectum and sustain injuries like this very bright-minded pledge did.
vocab.tip: Learn rectum as a precise anatomy label and stress REC-. Distinguish the rectum inside the body from the anus, the opening.
vocab.example: The diagram labels the rectum.
vocab.example_cn: 图中标出了直肠。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Anatomical vocabulary needed to understand the reported injury; no procedural instruction.

vocab.definition: to suffer or experience an injury or loss
vocab.source_excerpt: Also, you could tear your rectum and sustain injuries like this very bright-minded pledge did.
vocab.tip: Sustain can mean keep going, but sustain an injury means suffer it. Memorize the whole verb-object pair instead of using one translation everywhere.
vocab.example: The building sustained damage during the storm.
vocab.example_cn: 这栋建筑在暴风雨中遭到损坏。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Sustain injuries is the suffer sense, not support or maintain.

vocab.definition: platforms projecting from a building above ground level, usually with railings
vocab.source_excerpt: Sometimes there will be a bunk bed next to an open window and they'll be intoxicated, roll out of the bed and then roll out the window, fall from fire escapes, fall from balconies.
vocab.tip: balcony changes y to -ies in the plural balconies. Picture several small platforms along a building.
vocab.example: The apartments have small balconies.
vocab.example_cn: 这些公寓都有小阳台。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Plural building structures in the list of fall locations.

vocab.definition: affected by alcohol or another substance, especially drunk
vocab.cn: 醉酒的；受酒精等影响的
vocab.source_excerpt: They fall off of roofs while intoxicated.
vocab.tip: Connect intoxicate with toxic to recall a substance affecting the body. Intoxicated is formal; drunk is the everyday equivalent in this passage.
vocab.example: The report said the driver appeared intoxicated.
vocab.example_cn: 报告称，司机看起来处于醉酒状态。
vocab.context_review_note: Alcohol context; teaching example retains reported appearance rather than a diagnosis.

vocab.definition: an arrangement that provides financial protection against specified risks
vocab.source_excerpt: Insurance companies, at least in my personal experience, they don't like to say no to coverage because that's saying no to money.
vocab.tip: Connect insure with insurance: insure is the action, insurance the protection. Distinguish insure a car from ensure that something happens.
vocab.example: We bought insurance for the trip.
vocab.example_cn: 我们为这次旅行买了保险。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The narrator generalizes from personal experience; retain this as language study, not a factual recommendation about policies.

vocab.definition: people or organizations bringing civil court cases against others
vocab.source_excerpt: I mean, there are like a lot of branding gone wrong where plaintiffs need skin grafts in extreme cases because they were branded by some sort of hot iron tool.
vocab.tip: plaintiff ends in /f/, so plural -s is /s/. Compare plaintiffs, who bring a case, with defendants, who answer it.
vocab.example: The lawyer represented the plaintiffs.
vocab.example_cn: 这名律师代理原告方。
vocab.context_review_note: Plural legal role; filing a claim does not establish its truth.

vocab.definition: cases brought before a court by people or organizations against others
vocab.source_excerpt: Imagine the amount of- Lawsuits, liability.
vocab.tip: law + suit gives lawsuit, a legal action; plural -s makes lawsuits. A suit here is not clothing.
vocab.example: The company faced several lawsuits.
vocab.example_cn: 该公司面临数起诉讼。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Fragment completes imagine the amount of; teaching model uses several/countable cases rather than copying disfluency.

vocab.definition: brought a legal claim against someone in court; in passive use, faced such a claim
vocab.source_excerpt: That fraternities usually get sued for, such as hazing, alcohol violations, or essay.
vocab.tip: sue already ends in e, so add only d: sued. Contrast sued /sud/ with suit /sut/ by listening to the final consonant.
vocab.example: The company was sued for damages.
vocab.example_cn: 该公司被起诉要求赔偿损失。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Get sued is passive; does not imply the claimant won.

vocab.definition: planned or arranged as a coordinated activity
vocab.source_excerpt: You got hazed in ways that probably have a lot more in common with organized FetLife meetups.
vocab.tip: organize + d gives organized. Here it describes a planned event, while an organized person is good at arranging things.
vocab.example: The volunteers attended an organized training session.
vocab.example_cn: 志愿者们参加了一场统一安排的培训。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Modifies meetups; comparison is the narrator's criticism, not a factual equivalence between all events.

vocab.definition: alternative ways of dealing with problems or restrictions
vocab.source_excerpt: There are two odd workarounds for this alcohol thing.
vocab.tip: workaround is one alternative route; workarounds are several. The plural ending is /z/ after /d/.
vocab.example: We tested two possible workarounds.
vocab.example_cn: 我们测试了两种可能的变通办法。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary + transparent inflection/abbreviation rule
vocab.context_review_note: Two arrangements in the source; no implication that these always meet insurance conditions.

vocab.definition: a person invited to an event or welcomed by a host
vocab.source_excerpt: And it's like a guest list.
vocab.tip: Pair guest with host: the host welcomes, the guest visits. Keep the final /st/ and distinguish guest from guess.
vocab.example: Each guest received a name tag.
vocab.example_cn: 每位来宾都领到了一张姓名牌。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Invited event attendee, not specifically a hotel customer.

vocab.definition: usual or generally accepted as normal
vocab.source_excerpt: I mean, it's not, I don't know if it's standard for a lot of fraternities, but it seems to be a thing.
vocab.tip: Stand a regular example beside unusual ones: it is the standard. Learn standard practice to recall the adjective sense.
vocab.example: Checking the list is standard practice.
vocab.example_cn: 核对名单是惯常做法。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The speaker explicitly does not know whether the practice is standard, so avoid converting it into a universal claim.

vocab.definition: a sequence of actions or events through which something happens
vocab.source_excerpt: However police found circumstantial evidence in the fraternity house including evidence that the patient may have lost control of his bowels in the process and defecated on himself which he also has no recollection of
vocab.tip: Remember process as steps happening one after another. In the process can mean while that was happening, without implying a formal procedure.
vocab.example: The box was damaged in the process of moving it.
vocab.example_cn: 箱子在搬运过程中损坏了。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Temporal phrase within the alleged events, not a legal summons or software process.

vocab.definition: drinks, especially when described formally
vocab.source_excerpt: You can only bring like six beverages, like six beers and under, or like one bottle of wine.
vocab.tip: beverage is a formal word for drink; its /dʒ/ ending takes plural /ɪz/. Count drinks, not types, in six beverages.
vocab.example: The cafe serves hot and cold beverages.
vocab.example_cn: 这家咖啡馆供应冷热饮品。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Six beverages refers to number of drinks, not 六种饮料; source lists beer/wine quantities as an example.

vocab.definition: a route or means of getting out of danger, here part of fire escape
vocab.cn: 逃生通道；（fire escape）消防逃生梯
vocab.source_excerpt: Sometimes there will be a bunk bed next to an open window and they'll be intoxicated, roll out of the bed and then roll out the window, fall from fire escapes, fall from balconies.
vocab.tip: Escape means get out of danger; a fire escape is the structure used to do that. Learn the whole compound so fire does not become the thing escaping.
vocab.example: The building has an external fire escape.
vocab.example_cn: 这栋楼有外置消防逃生梯。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Noun within fire escapes, not the standalone verb escape in this sentence.

vocab.definition: removes someone from a group, plan, or arrangement
vocab.cn: 取消某人的资格；将某人移出
vocab.source_excerpt: If you sue a fraternity member and their fraternity drops them from their insurance, what happens then?
vocab.tip: Drop can mean let something fall; figuratively, drop someone from a plan removes them. Drops here is a verb, not plural droplets.
vocab.example: The organization drops members who stop paying fees.
vocab.example_cn: 该组织会取消不再缴费者的成员资格。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Corrects plural-of-drop definition and 退出 meaning: the organization removes the member, rather than the member voluntarily quitting.

vocab.definition: to take on a duty or responsibility
vocab.source_excerpt: Two usually approved ways of drinking at fraternity houses that have your chance of most likely staying insured by the fraternity insurance is one, the fraternity brings in a third party vendor to check IDs and they assume the liability.
vocab.tip: Assume has two common senses: assume it is true means suppose; assume responsibility means take it on. Picture putting a responsibility on your own shoulders.
vocab.example: The team leader will assume responsibility for the project.
vocab.example_cn: 团队负责人将承担项目责任。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Responsibility-taking sense in assume the liability, not guessing or believing without evidence.

vocab.definition: producing a useful or favorable effect
vocab.source_excerpt: It's deeply financially beneficial for a lot of these institutions.
vocab.tip: benefit becomes beneficial. The -cial ending sounds /ʃəl/; connect the adjective with a benefit received.
vocab.example: The change could be beneficial to students.
vocab.example_cn: 这项改变可能对学生有益。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Financial advantage alleged for institutions, not necessarily moral or educational benefit.

vocab.definition: made information known that was previously private or unknown
vocab.source_excerpt: And most of them are not disclosed.
vocab.tip: disclose + d gives disclosed. Link disclose with reveal; contrast disclosed with undisclosed to remember the negative prefix un-.
vocab.example: The full amount was not disclosed.
vocab.example_cn: 完整金额没有被披露。
vocab.context_review_note: Source refers to donations; not disclosed does not itself imply illegality.

vocab.definition: money or goods given to support a person or organization
vocab.source_excerpt: Is it donations?
vocab.tip: donate drops final e before -ion: donation. The donor gives; the donation is what is given.
vocab.example: They made a donation to the scholarship fund.
vocab.example_cn: 他们向奖学金基金捐了款。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Financial contributions to institutions; no actual amount or donor identity verified.

vocab.definition: attractive enough to make someone want something
vocab.source_excerpt: That is more enticing to someone than getting student loans for whatever degree that they want.
vocab.tip: entice drops final e before -ing: enticing. Enticing describes the attraction; enticed describes the person drawn in.
vocab.example: The flexible schedule made the offer more enticing.
vocab.example_cn: 灵活的时间安排让这份提议更有吸引力。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Speaker sarcastically contrasts party attractions with academic costs; not an endorsement of dangerous activities.

vocab.definition: in relation to money or financial resources
vocab.source_excerpt: It's deeply financially beneficial for a lot of these institutions.
vocab.tip: financial + -ly gives financially. It answers in what respect: financially beneficial means beneficial in money terms.
vocab.example: The project is financially sustainable.
vocab.example_cn: 这个项目在财务上可以持续运转。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Narrows beneficial to monetary benefit, not overall social value.

vocab.definition: the fraternity and sorority system and associated social activities at US colleges
vocab.cn: 美国大学兄弟会、姐妹会体系及其社交生活
vocab.source_excerpt: Even Cornell University, a lot of students are trying to ban Greek life.

collocations.meaning_zh: 参与兄弟会或姐妹会活动

vocab.tip: Greek points to Greek-letter organization names, not Greece as a location. Picture letter-named campus organizations to recall Greek life.
vocab.mental_image_zh: 参与兄弟会或姐妹会活动
vocab.example: She wrote an article about Greek life on campus.
vocab.example_cn: 她写了一篇有关校园兄弟会和姐妹会生活的文章。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Corrects literal 希腊生活 interpretation; covers both fraternity and sorority organizations.

vocab.definition: homes or accommodation provided for people
vocab.source_excerpt: For student housing.
vocab.tip: house becomes housing, with /z/ in the middle and no final e. Housing is usually uncountable, unlike individual houses.
vocab.example: The university plans to expand student housing.
vocab.example_cn: 大学计划增加学生住宿设施。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Accommodation, not a machine casing.

vocab.definition: something that encourages a person or organization to act
vocab.source_excerpt: And also on top of that, there is a bottom line incentive.
vocab.tip: Pair incentive with incentive to + verb: a benefit creates a reason to act. Picture a reward attached to an action.
vocab.example: Lower costs provide an incentive to share resources.
vocab.example_cn: 降低成本为共享资源提供了动力。
vocab.context_review_note: Bottom-line incentive is a financial motivation, not an instruction or guaranteed result.

vocab.definition: an established organization such as a university
vocab.source_excerpt: It's deeply financially beneficial for a lot of these institutions.
vocab.tip: Institute and institution belong to the same word family. In this passage, picture a university rather than an abstract social custom.
vocab.example: The institution offers several scholarship programs.
vocab.example_cn: 这所机构提供多项奖学金计划。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Refers to colleges/universities, not hospitalization or a custom.

vocab.definition: to keep something in good condition through regular care
vocab.source_excerpt: One random one that I hadn't even thought of was a lot of these universities, they don't have to build and maintain more buildings anymore.
vocab.tip: maintenance is the noun related to maintain. Keep the second syllable stressed in maintain and picture regular repairs that keep a building usable.
vocab.example: The school pays to maintain the buildings.
vocab.example_cn: 学校支付建筑维护费用。
vocab.context_review_note: Building upkeep, not asserting an opinion or maintaining innocence.

vocab.definition: activities used to promote something and attract customers or users
vocab.source_excerpt: But there is also, some people say it could be the marketing aspect.
vocab.tip: market + -ing names the activity of reaching a market. Here prospective students are the audience, not shoppers at a street market.
vocab.example: The team discussed its marketing strategy.
vocab.example_cn: 团队讨论了营销策略。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Attracting students through social-life appeal, as proposed by the speaker.

vocab.definition: people who formerly attended or graduated from a school or university
vocab.source_excerpt: But also alumni who are part of Greek life seem to, at least according to one research done, seem more financially generous to their alma maters later in life if they were part of Greek life.
vocab.tip: Alumni is a traditional plural: alumnus is singular masculine, alumna feminine. Remember the plural ending sounds /naɪ/ and use alumni are.
vocab.example: Many alumni returned for the reunion.
vocab.example_cn: 许多校友回来参加了聚会。
vocab.context_review_note: Former students, not current students or aluminum; the alleged donation finding remains attributed.

vocab.definition: a local branch of a larger organization
vocab.source_excerpt: So these institutions are now saving money since Greek life and the chapter houses typically reduce the number of students that need campus housing.
vocab.tip: A chapter is one part of a whole: in a book a section, in an organization a local branch. Here houses anchors the branch sense.
vocab.example: The chapter rents a house near campus.
vocab.example_cn: 这个分会在校园附近租了一栋房子。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Same branch sense as Unit 4, separately retained for this Unit's housing context.

vocab.definition: buildings or rooms where students live, short for dormitories
vocab.source_excerpt: So that means less buildings, less insurance the school has to pay for those student dorms because it's like by bed and by student.
vocab.tip: Dorm is the shortened form of dormitory. Add plural -s /z/ after /m/: dorms.
vocab.example: Most first-year students live in the dorms.
vocab.example_cn: 大多数一年级学生住在宿舍。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Student accommodation, not classrooms; source's less buildings is not copied into the teaching model.

vocab.definition: combined to become one organization or whole
vocab.source_excerpt: Apparently, it was three separate organizations that merged into one.
vocab.tip: merge already ends in e, so add d: merged. Keep /dʒd/ at the end; picture two groups becoming one.
vocab.example: The two departments merged into one.
vocab.example_cn: 两个部门合并成了一个。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Historical claim reported with apparently; no independent verification of the organizations' dates.

vocab.definition: money paid for instruction at a school or university
vocab.source_excerpt: It also allows institutions to expand the number of students they can admit, which means more tuition.
vocab.tip: Connect tuition with tutor: both relate to teaching. In American college context tuition usually means the price of instruction, not housing costs.
vocab.example: The scholarship covers tuition but not housing.
vocab.example_cn: 奖学金支付学费，但不支付住宿费。
vocab.context_review_note: More tuition means increased tuition revenue from more admitted students, not more teaching sessions.

vocab.definition: local branches of an organization that are currently operating
vocab.source_excerpt: The entire fraternity has about 48 active chapters across the United States.

collocations.meaning_zh: 全国各地仍在运作的分会

vocab.tip: Active means operating, not simply energetic; chapters are local branches. Picture a map with the currently operating branches lit up.
vocab.example: The organization has active chapters in several cities.
vocab.example_cn: 该组织在多个城市设有仍在运作的分会。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The approximate count is a recorded claim, not a live organizational total.

vocab.definition: having the eyes covered so that one cannot see
vocab.source_excerpt: He alleges that he's sleep deprived, physically exhausted, and quote, I was blindfolded and tossed onto a sheet, flinging me up and down.
vocab.tip: blindfold + -ed adds /ɪd/ after /d/. Connect the noun blindfold, the cloth, with the state blindfolded.
vocab.example: The participant was blindfolded during the game.
vocab.example_cn: 游戏过程中，这名参与者被蒙住了眼睛。
vocab.context_review_note: Passive state in an attributed account; no staging of the harmful initiation in the teaching example.

vocab.definition: not having enough of something necessary or desirable
vocab.source_excerpt: He alleges that he's sleep deprived, physically exhausted, and quote, I was blindfolded and tossed onto a sheet, flinging me up and down.
vocab.tip: deprive drops final e before -ed: deprived. Remember deprived of something, and the compound sleep-deprived.
vocab.example: After the long journey, we felt sleep-deprived.
vocab.example_cn: 长途旅行之后，我们觉得睡眠不足。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Sleep deprivation in the source, not necessarily economic deprivation.

vocab.definition: to continue through something difficult or painful
vocab.source_excerpt: Fully fledged, fully pledged Chi Phi member if they can just endure the next few hours.
vocab.tip: Connect endure with endurance: the ability to keep going through difficulty. Stress the second syllable.
vocab.example: They had to endure a long delay.
vocab.example_cn: 他们不得不忍受长时间的延误。
vocab.context_review_note: Conditional ability to get through the next hours, not approval that participants should accept harm.

vocab.definition: a student in the first year of high school or university in the US
vocab.source_excerpt: OK, and he says that when he was a freshman, he had endured months of physical, emotional and psychological damage.
vocab.tip: Fresh suggests new; freshman is a new first-year student. Plural freshmen changes man to men, while freshman year keeps the singular modifier.
vocab.example: She joined the club during her freshman year.
vocab.example_cn: 她在大一时加入了这个社团。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: First university year in this account, not a gender restriction on the student's identity.

vocab.definition: a process or ceremony through which someone joins a group
vocab.source_excerpt: And I guess they're all like on the this is the night of the initiation.
vocab.tip: initiate drops final e and adds -ion: initiation. Connect initial, the beginning, with the start of membership.
vocab.example: The club held a short initiation ceremony.
vocab.example_cn: 俱乐部举行了一场简短的入会仪式。
vocab.context_review_note: Initiation does not inherently mean hazing; the specific harmful conduct is alleged separately.

vocab.definition: extremely tired in the body
vocab.source_excerpt: He alleges that he's sleep deprived, physically exhausted, and quote, I was blindfolded and tossed onto a sheet, flinging me up and down.
vocab.tip: physical + -ly specifies the body; exhausted means used up, like an exhausted supply. Picture bodily energy depleted.
vocab.example: After the move, I felt physically exhausted.
vocab.example_cn: 搬家之后，我感到身体筋疲力尽。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Bodily fatigue in the attributed account, distinct from emotional exhaustion.

vocab.definition: committed to joining a fraternity or having gone through its pledge process
vocab.cn: 已承诺入会的；经历入会过程的
vocab.source_excerpt: Fully fledged, fully pledged Chi Phi member if they can just endure the next few hours.
vocab.tip: pledge adds only d because it ends in e: pledged. Keep the /dʒd/ ending; don't add a separate vowel.
vocab.example: He pledged a fraternity in his first year.
vocab.example_cn: 他大一时报名加入了一个兄弟会。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Source says fully fledged, fully pledged as wordplay/self-repair. Fully fledged means fully established; fully pledged is not a universal formal membership category.

vocab.definition: the edge of a steep drop; figuratively, a point just before a major change
vocab.cn: 悬崖边缘；重大变化的边缘
vocab.source_excerpt: They're all on the precipice of becoming a.
vocab.tip: Picture a person at a cliff edge to remember precipice. On the precipice of + -ing suggests being very close to a consequential change.
vocab.example: The company was on the precipice of a major change.
vocab.example_cn: 公司正处于重大变化的关口。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Source metaphor refers to impending membership and continues into 340; no literal cliff.

vocab.definition: relating to the mind, feelings, or mental processes
vocab.source_excerpt: OK, and he says that when he was a freshman, he had endured months of physical, emotional and psychological damage.
vocab.tip: psychology becomes psychological. Initial ps sounds /s/; connect the word with mental experience rather than physical injury.
vocab.example: The report discussed the psychological effects of the event.
vocab.example_cn: 报告讨论了这一事件的心理影响。
vocab.context_review_note: Reported mental harm, not a diagnosis established by this review.

vocab.definition: connected to and useful for understanding the matter being discussed
vocab.source_excerpt: So this is not even happening during this Jane Doe case, but this is highly relevant.
vocab.tip: Learn relevant to + topic, not relevant with. Imagine sorting information into connected and unrelated piles.
vocab.example: Please include only information relevant to the question.
vocab.example_cn: 请只加入与这个问题相关的信息。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Earlier separate experience is said to be relevant, not part of the same alleged event.

vocab.definition: to express an idea or feeling clearly in words
vocab.source_excerpt: But inside, I was ashamed of my vulnerability and unable to articulate or process the pain I was in.
vocab.tip: The verb articulate ends in /leɪt/; the adjective articulate has a reduced ending. Here unable to requires the verb: put feelings into words.
vocab.example: She found it difficult to articulate her concerns.
vocab.example_cn: 她发现很难清楚表达自己的担忧。
vocab.context_review_note: Verb for expression, not the adjective describing an eloquent person.

vocab.definition: feeling distress or embarrassment about oneself or something one has done or experienced
vocab.source_excerpt: But inside, I was ashamed of my vulnerability and unable to articulate or process the pain I was in.
vocab.tip: Shame is the feeling; ashamed describes the person feeling it. Use ashamed of + noun/-ing, not ashamed for everything.
vocab.example: He felt ashamed of hiding the mistake.
vocab.example_cn: 他为隐瞒这个错误感到羞愧。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The speaker reports shame about vulnerability; this does not imply he was responsible for harm done to him.

vocab.definition: a pungent red pepper used as a spice, usually in powdered form
vocab.source_excerpt: He says mung consisted of cold oatmeal, vinegar, hot sauce, and cayenne pepper.
vocab.tip: Remember the two beats kai-EN, stressing the second. Anchor the unusual spelling cayenne to the spice label cayenne pepper.
vocab.example: The recipe calls for a pinch of cayenne pepper.
vocab.example_cn: 食谱要求加入少许卡宴辣椒粉。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Ingredient named in the account; teaching example uses ordinary food preparation, not harmful application.

vocab.definition: a box in which a dead person is placed for burial
vocab.source_excerpt: I was set in a coffin and lowered through a trap door into a secret chapter room where I was officially inducted into the fraternity.
vocab.tip: Remember double f in coffin by picturing the two long sides of a box. It is a burial box, not coffee.
vocab.example: The museum displayed an old wooden coffin.
vocab.example_cn: 博物馆展出了一口古老的木棺。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Object in an attributed initiation account; the account does not describe the person as dead.

vocab.definition: formally admitted into an organization or role
vocab.cn: 被正式接纳入会；被引入某职务
vocab.source_excerpt: I was set in a coffin and lowered through a trap door into a secret chapter room where I was officially inducted into the fraternity.
vocab.tip: induct ends in /t/, so inducted adds /ɪd/. Link induction with the formal moment of joining, followed by into.
vocab.example: The new members were inducted into the club.
vocab.example_cn: 新成员被正式接纳加入俱乐部。
vocab.context_review_note: Formal admission, not the unrelated scientific induction sense.

vocab.definition: causing someone to suffer harm, pain, or an unwanted burden
vocab.source_excerpt: Smeared all over his genitals but he did not consent to anyone touching him or inflicting this amount of pain he says i screamed bloody murder
vocab.tip: Learn inflict harm on someone as a complete pattern. The harm is the object; on introduces the affected person.
vocab.example: The report accused the group of inflicting emotional harm.
vocab.example_cn: 报告指责该团体造成了心理伤害。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The account explicitly says he did not consent; attribution remains intact.

vocab.definition: a small door in a floor or ceiling giving access to another space
vocab.cn: 地板或天花板上的活板门
vocab.source_excerpt: I was set in a coffin and lowered through a trap door into a secret chapter room where I was officially inducted into the fraternity.
vocab.tip: Trap door names a hidden or horizontal access door. Picture a panel opening in a floor, not a door meant to catch an animal.
vocab.example: A trap door led to the storage space below.
vocab.example_cn: 一扇活板门通向下面的储物空间。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Physical access opening, not a metaphorical trap.

vocab.definition: a sour liquid used in cooking or preserving food
vocab.source_excerpt: He says mung consisted of cold oatmeal, vinegar, hot sauce, and cayenne pepper.
vocab.tip: Say vinegar in three beats, VIN-uh-ger, with the stress first. Anchor it to the sour taste of a bottle of vinegar.
vocab.example: Add a little vinegar to the dressing.
vocab.example_cn: 在调味汁里加一点醋。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Ingredient vocabulary; everyday food example avoids reenacting the alleged abuse.

vocab.definition: the state of being exposed to harm or emotional hurt
vocab.source_excerpt: But inside, I was ashamed of my vulnerability and unable to articulate or process the pain I was in.
vocab.tip: vulnerable changes -able to -ability: vulnerability. Connect being vulnerable with needing care, not being at fault.
vocab.example: She spoke openly about her sense of vulnerability.
vocab.example_cn: 她坦率地谈到了自己的脆弱感。
vocab.context_review_note: Personal feeling in the quoted account; no blame is assigned for being vulnerable.

vocab.definition: the band of fabric around the waist of trousers, shorts, or a skirt
vocab.source_excerpt: Hands reached under the waistband of my basketball shorts and slathered fistfuls of spicy mung all over my genitals.
vocab.tip: waist + band gives waistband: a band around the waist. Distinguish waist from waste by picturing clothing.
vocab.example: These shorts have an elastic waistband.
vocab.example_cn: 这条短裤有松紧腰头。
vocab.ipa_source: freedictionaryapi.com (Wiktionary-derived)
vocab.context_review_note: Clothing part in the quoted account; teaching example remains neutral.

vocab.definition: a condition involving compulsive dependence on a substance or activity
vocab.source_excerpt: Along with the social license to frame addiction as valor and sexual conquest as glory.
vocab.tip: Connect addicted with addiction: the adjective describes dependence and the noun names the condition. Stress -DIC-.
vocab.example: The article discussed support for people struggling with addiction.
vocab.example_cn: 文章讨论了如何支持受成瘾问题困扰的人。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The quoted criticism concerns glorifying dependence; no diagnosis of a named person.

vocab.definition: the act of gaining control or a victory; here, a boastful way of treating sexual partners as achievements
vocab.cn: 征服；（此处）把性关系当作战绩
vocab.source_excerpt: Along with the social license to frame addiction as valor and sexual conquest as glory.
vocab.tip: Connect conquest with conquer: both evoke winning control. Sexual conquest applies a victory metaphor to people and can be objectifying.
vocab.example: The essay criticized the language of sexual conquest.
vocab.example_cn: 这篇文章批评了把性关系描述为征服战绩的说法。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Critically quoted objectifying framing, not a term the lesson endorses as a positive social goal.

vocab.definition: thrown away or left because no longer wanted
vocab.source_excerpt: And now in one of the now-vacant rooms, a very important room for this case, one video shows someone walking through this empty room and there's garbage, leftover food everywhere, discarded furniture.
vocab.tip: discard means throw away; after its final /d/, -ed is /ɪd/. Picture items set aside for disposal.
vocab.example: Discarded furniture filled the empty room.
vocab.example_cn: 空房间里堆满了废弃家具。
vocab.context_review_note: Unwanted objects shown in a video, not evidence establishing why they were left.

vocab.definition: great honor, praise, or admiration
vocab.source_excerpt: Along with the social license to frame addiction as valor and sexual conquest as glory.
vocab.tip: Glory names the praise; glorious describes something seen as splendid. In the source, the speaker criticizes what the group treats as glory.
vocab.example: The team valued cooperation more than personal glory.
vocab.example_cn: 团队重视合作，胜过个人荣耀。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Part of a critical framing contrast; not approval of sexual conquest.

vocab.definition: things made available or offered to people
vocab.source_excerpt: I accepted the fraternity's offerings of access to drugs, alcohol, and girls, but
vocab.tip: offer + -ing makes an offering, something offered; plural offerings can mean services or opportunities, not only religious gifts.
vocab.example: The center expanded its educational offerings.
vocab.example_cn: 这个中心增加了教育项目。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Access to substances and social opportunities in the account, not religious sacrifice.

vocab.definition: not occupied or currently in use
vocab.source_excerpt: But it's interesting to know that the house that Jared helped plan this great fratsby party, the Kai-Fi house, is now vacant.
vocab.tip: Connect vacant with vacancy: an unoccupied room has a vacancy. Picture an empty room rather than an available holiday.
vocab.example: The building has been vacant for months.
vocab.example_cn: 这栋楼已经空置了几个月。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Occupancy at the video's/recording's time, not a live status check.

vocab.definition: the act of police taking someone into custody
vocab.source_excerpt: There is an arrest made for ketamine at a fraternity at Chi Phi, to be exact, a drug related arrest at the same exact house.
vocab.tip: An arrest stops a person's freedom of movement; learn make an arrest for the police action. Arrested does not mean convicted.
vocab.example: Police confirmed that an arrest had been made.
vocab.example_cn: 警方证实已经实施了一次逮捕。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Narrator says an arrest was logged but does not identify the exact offense or person.

vocab.definition: a record listing reported criminal incidents
vocab.cn: 犯罪事件记录；治安事件日志
vocab.source_excerpt: There's like a crime log that they have, like a daily crime log.
vocab.tip: Log here means a written record, not wood. Pair crime with log to picture dated entries of reported incidents.
vocab.example: The campus website publishes a daily crime log.
vocab.example_cn: 校园网站发布每日治安事件记录。
vocab.context_review_note: A log records reports/incidents; it is not a list of convictions.

vocab.definition: temporary, while waiting for a final decision or arrangement
vocab.source_excerpt: Now, the university does not place the fraternity on some sort of like interim suspension because they're going to host another party that day.
vocab.tip: Think of an interval between stages: interim fills the gap until a final arrangement. It does not mean permanent or final.
vocab.example: The team appointed an interim manager.
vocab.example_cn: 团队任命了一位临时经理。
vocab.context_review_note: Temporary measure pending investigation, not a final disciplinary outcome.

vocab.definition: the authority to make decisions or apply rules in a particular area or matter
vocab.source_excerpt: So it's not off campus housing, which means it's technically under the jurisdiction of Cornell, right?
vocab.tip: The juris- family connects with law, as in jurisprudence. Learn under the jurisdiction of + authority to remember who has power to decide.
vocab.example: The matter falls within the committee's jurisdiction.
vocab.example_cn: 这件事属于委员会的权限范围。
vocab.context_review_note: Narrator's assertion about campus authority, not a legal determination that location alone settles jurisdiction.

vocab.definition: a drug used medically as an anesthetic and also used illicitly
vocab.source_excerpt: There is an arrest made for ketamine at a fraternity at Chi Phi, to be exact, a drug related arrest at the same exact house.

collocations.meaning_zh: 涉及氯胺酮的违法事件

vocab.tip: Say ketamine in three beats, KET-uh-meen. Treat it as a specific drug name, not a synonym for every anesthetic or illicit substance.
vocab.mental_image_zh: 涉及氯胺酮的违法事件
vocab.example: The report referred to a ketamine-related arrest.
vocab.example_cn: 报告提到了一次与氯胺酮有关的逮捕。
vocab.ipa_source: freedictionaryapi.com (Wiktionary-derived)
vocab.context_review_note: Reported substance name only; no dosage, use instructions or determination of the exact offense.

vocab.definition: took an amount of a drug greater than the body could safely tolerate
vocab.source_excerpt: When you go through little snippets of the Title IX investigation, which is the Jane Doe investigation that we're going to kind of get into in a second, there are allegations that someone overdosed.
vocab.tip: over- means too much; dose is an amount. Overdose adds d to become overdosed, with final /st/ rather than a new syllable.
vocab.example: The report alleged that someone had overdosed.
vocab.example_cn: 报告称有人药物摄入过量。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Source calls this an allegation and says the relation to the arrest is unknown; do not merge identities or establish a diagnosis.

vocab.definition: the state of having or controlling something
vocab.source_excerpt: So we don't know if it was the same individual, if it was two different individuals, if someone is supplying and then someone overdosed or if someone overdosed and that's how they found out that they were in possession of ketamine.
vocab.tip: possess becomes possession; keep the double s in both places. Possession means having/control, not necessarily legal ownership.
vocab.example: She was in possession of the original document.
vocab.example_cn: 她持有原始文件。
vocab.context_review_note: Having the substance is distinct from supplying it; source presents alternatives, not a settled account.

vocab.definition: courteous, honorable, and considerate in a traditional ideal of conduct
vocab.cn: 有骑士风度的；礼貌而重荣誉的
vocab.source_excerpt: Chivalrous behavior crosses the ages to touch the heart of Chi Phi.
vocab.tip: Connect chivalrous with chivalry, the knightly ideal. Initial ch is /ʃ/, unlike chair; picture an old-fashioned courtesy.
vocab.example: The story describes a chivalrous gesture.
vocab.example_cn: 故事描述了一个有骑士风度的举动。
vocab.ipa_source: freedictionaryapi.com (Wiktionary-derived)
vocab.context_review_note: Quoted ideal in a creed; no judgment that the organization lived up to it.

vocab.definition: a statement of beliefs or principles held by a group or person
vocab.source_excerpt: They have a creed of Kai-Fai and it reads in short, I believe in the friendship of Kai-Fai, whether on the road or in the chapter house, the hand of brotherhood is always extended.
vocab.tip: The long ee in creed sounds /i/. Picture a short written set of beliefs; distinguish creed from greed, desire for more.
vocab.example: The group's creed emphasizes honesty.
vocab.example_cn: 该团体的信条强调诚实。
vocab.context_review_note: Institutional belief statement, not a legal code or a proven description of conduct.

vocab.definition: a person's honesty and consistency with moral principles
vocab.source_excerpt: Their founding principles they state are truth, honor, and personal integrity.
vocab.tip: Integrity can mean wholeness; personal integrity connects actions and principles into a consistent whole. Remember acting honestly even when unobserved.
vocab.example: Her colleagues respected her personal integrity.
vocab.example_cn: 同事们尊重她的个人操守。
vocab.context_review_note: Stated founding ideal, not a factual certification of any member's character.

vocab.definition: special permissions or benefits available to a person or group
vocab.source_excerpt: We're not kicking people out, but we're just going to investigate and you guys lose your privileges of throwing fucking ragers and doing keg stands.
vocab.tip: Privilege ends in /dʒ/, so privileges adds /ɪz/. Here permissions can be withdrawn; do not equate every privilege with a universal right.
vocab.example: Members can lose their booking privileges.
vocab.example_cn: 成员可能会失去预约权限。
vocab.context_review_note: Party-hosting permissions in imagined institutional response; not a confirmed sanction in that sentence.

vocab.definition: a name used instead of a person's real name
vocab.source_excerpt: 20 year old Jane Doe, this is obviously a pseudonym, but Jane Doe shares the relevant details of her starting at Cornell in her civil lawsuit.
vocab.tip: pseudo- means false or assumed and -onym relates to name. Initial p is silent: SOO-duh-nim.
vocab.example: The author published the article under a pseudonym.
vocab.example_cn: 作者以化名发表了这篇文章。
vocab.context_review_note: Jane Doe is identified as an assumed name; no attempt to identify the person behind it.

vocab.definition: a second-year student in a US high school or university
vocab.source_excerpt: Instead, 22 hours later, a sophomore, 20-year-old Jane Doe alleges that she went to Chi Phi for a party and was gang raped at the fraternity house for seven hours.
vocab.tip: Learn the sequence freshman → sophomore → junior → senior. Attach sophomore to year two instead of guessing age from the word.
vocab.example: She changed her major during her sophomore year.
vocab.example_cn: 她在大二时换了专业。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Academic year, not a guarantee of exactly two completed years; the narrator's timeline remains attributed.

vocab.definition: a group connected by a place, institution, or shared interests
vocab.source_excerpt: So she joins the sorority because she felt like when she got to Cornell, they kept promoting Greek life as like a very vital part of the campus community.
vocab.tip: Common and community suggest something shared. Here the shared connection is campus life, not necessarily one residential neighborhood.
vocab.example: The event brought the campus community together.
vocab.example_cn: 这场活动把校园里的师生群体聚到了一起。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Campus social group, not an online-platform feature or a geographic town alone.

vocab.definition: encouraging interest in or support for something
vocab.source_excerpt: So she joins the sorority because she felt like when she got to Cornell, they kept promoting Greek life as like a very vital part of the campus community.
vocab.tip: promote drops final e before -ing. Promoting an activity increases interest; promoting an employee gives a higher job, a different sense.
vocab.example: The club is promoting its new activities.
vocab.example_cn: 这个社团正在宣传新活动。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Encouraging Greek-life participation as reported by the speaker, not promoting someone to a higher position.

vocab.definition: willing to give more money, help, or resources than expected
vocab.source_excerpt: But also alumni who are part of Greek life seem to, at least according to one research done, seem more financially generous to their alma maters later in life if they were part of Greek life.
vocab.tip: Connect generous with generosity: the adjective describes the giver, the noun the quality. Anchor both to giving rather than the unrelated general.
vocab.example: The alumni were generous with their support.
vocab.example_cn: 校友们慷慨地提供了支持。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Financial giving to former universities; source's research claim remains qualified, not independently established.

vocab.definition: relating to the body rather than the mind
vocab.source_excerpt: OK, and he says that when he was a freshman, he had endured months of physical, emotional and psychological damage.
vocab.tip: Physical begins with ph pronounced /f/. Contrast physical with psychological in the source's list of harms.
vocab.example: The job involves physical effort.
vocab.example_cn: 这份工作需要体力劳动。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Body-related harm, not the separate sense of a tangible object.

vocab.definition: officially prevented from entering or taking part
vocab.source_excerpt: The Xi chapter actually of Chi Phi at Cornell has been barred from campus after Jane Doe's incident.
vocab.tip: bar doubles r before -ed: barred. Picture a bar across an entrance; use barred from + place or -ing.
vocab.example: Visitors were barred from entering the closed area.
vocab.example_cn: 访客被禁止进入封闭区域。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Reported campus exclusion of a chapter; does not itself mean a criminal conviction.

vocab.definition: a temporary stopping of participation, activity, or permission
vocab.source_excerpt: Now, the university does not place the fraternity on some sort of like interim suspension because they're going to host another party that day.

collocations.meaning_zh: 暂停一个团体的活动资格

vocab.tip: Suspend becomes suspension, with /ʃ/ in -sion. Picture an activity paused while a decision is pending, not permanently ended.
vocab.mental_image_zh: 暂停一个团体的活动资格
vocab.example: The club was placed on temporary suspension.
vocab.example_cn: 该社团被暂时停止活动。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Organizational activity status, not necessarily suspension of each student's studies.

vocab.definition: providing something that another person needs or receives
vocab.source_excerpt: They arrested someone, maybe like supplying or?
vocab.tip: Supply keeps y before -ing: supplying. Follow supplying with the thing provided, then to the recipient if needed.
vocab.example: The company is supplying equipment to local schools.
vocab.example_cn: 这家公司正在向本地学校供应设备。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Supply of a substance is only speculated about in the source; not established as the arrest charge.

vocab.definition: honesty and adherence to consistent moral principles
vocab.source_excerpt: Their founding principles they state are truth, honor, and personal integrity.
vocab.tip: Connect integrity with being whole: principles and actions fit together. In this passage it is moral integrity, not data/file integrity.
vocab.example: We expect everyone to act with integrity.
vocab.example_cn: 我们希望每个人都以诚信行事。
vocab.context_review_note: Moral principle listed in the creed; not certification of actual behavior.

vocab.definition: to build relationships that may offer social or professional opportunities
vocab.source_excerpt: They were just, they made it seem like, oh, this is where you network and you make so many friends and it seems like a safe environment.
vocab.tip: A net links points; network as a verb links people. Here you network, rather than connect a computer to a network.
vocab.example: The event gives students a chance to network with alumni.
vocab.example_cn: 这场活动给学生提供了与校友建立联系的机会。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Verb about relationships, not a computer system or television network.

vocab.definition: currently operating or participating rather than inactive
vocab.source_excerpt: The entire fraternity has about 48 active chapters across the United States.
vocab.tip: act + -ive describes involvement or operation. Here active contrasts with closed or inactive, not merely physically energetic.
vocab.example: The group remains active in the community.
vocab.example_cn: 这个团体仍在社区中开展活动。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Operating-status adjective in the chapter count; no current total certified.

vocab.definition: to examine information carefully to find out what happened
vocab.source_excerpt: We're not kicking people out, but we're just going to investigate and you guys lose your privileges of throwing fucking ragers and doing keg stands.
vocab.tip: Connect investigate with investigation: drop final e and add -ion for the noun. Investigating gathers facts; it does not itself prove guilt.
vocab.example: The university said it would investigate the complaint.
vocab.example_cn: 大学表示将调查这起投诉。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Imagined institutional response introduced by the narrator; not an actual announcement newly verified here.

vocab.definition: a female student social organization at a US college or university
vocab.source_excerpt: There's this weird poster of a sorority.
vocab.tip: Sorority is the counterpart of fraternity in this campus context. Link it with sisterhood; stress -ROR-.
vocab.example: She joined a sorority during college.
vocab.example_cn: 她上大学时加入了一个姐妹会。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Organization pictured on a poster; membership in that photograph does not connect the people to the alleged incident.

vocab.definition: a potent synthetic opioid used medically for severe pain and also found in illicit drug supplies
vocab.cn: 芬太尼，一种强效合成阿片类药物
vocab.source_excerpt: There's a fentanyl test.
vocab.tip: Remember the three beats FEN-ta-nyl, stressing the first. This is a specific substance name, not a general word for all drugs.
vocab.example: The report mentioned a fentanyl test.
vocab.example_cn: 报告提到了一项芬太尼检测。
vocab.ipa_source: freedictionaryapi.com (Wiktionary-derived)
vocab.context_review_note: An object described in a video does not prove substance use, a test result or who used it. No testing/medical instructions supplied.

vocab.definition: to help an activity or process happen more easily
vocab.source_excerpt: They help operate the sorority house, plan the parties, facilitate, hire vendors.
vocab.tip: Connect facilitate with facility as something that makes an activity easier. A facilitator helps a group work, rather than doing every task personally.
vocab.example: The coordinator helped facilitate the discussion.
vocab.example_cn: 协调员协助推动了讨论。
vocab.context_review_note: One of the staff member's organizational tasks; source leaves the object unstated, so none is inserted into the quote.

vocab.definition: a trained or experienced person paid to do a job
vocab.source_excerpt: This is a hired professional.

collocations.meaning_zh: 与受雇的专业人员合作

vocab.tip: Hire means employ for payment; professional identifies a paid specialist. Distinguish this role from a student volunteer.
vocab.example: The repairs were handled by a hired professional.
vocab.example_cn: 维修由受雇的专业人员负责。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Source contrasts employee role with student peer; paid professional does not itself guarantee competence or conduct.

vocab.definition: a person responsible for managing a residential house or facility
vocab.source_excerpt: No, a house mom is kind of like a house director for a sorority.
vocab.tip: Director directs operations; house tells you the workplace. Picture someone managing residential facilities rather than directing a film.
vocab.example: The house director arranged the repairs.
vocab.example_cn: 宿舍主管安排了维修。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The narrator's explanation of house mom; not necessarily a university employee.

vocab.definition: the minimum age at which a person is legally permitted to drink alcohol in the relevant setting
vocab.source_excerpt: She's not of legal drinking age, but she's completely intoxicated as per her lawsuit, she alleges.
vocab.tip: Legal modifies the permitted age, not the type of drink. Learn of legal drinking age as a fixed description of eligibility.
vocab.example: The staff checked whether guests were of legal drinking age.
vocab.example_cn: 工作人员检查了来宾是否达到法定饮酒年龄。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Language gloss for the narrated setting; no jurisdiction-wide statement of current age exceptions or legal advice.

vocab.definition: relating to the practical running of an organization or activity
vocab.cn: 运营方面的；日常运作的
vocab.source_excerpt: Who is like the operational manager.
vocab.tip: operation + -al gives operational. Here it concerns day-to-day running; an operational machine has a different sense, functioning and ready to use.
vocab.example: The team discussed operational responsibilities.
vocab.example_cn: 团队讨论了运营职责。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Modifies manager in source; not a statement about equipment being functional.

vocab.definition: a manager responsible for an organization's everyday activities
vocab.cn: 运营经理；日常事务主管
vocab.source_excerpt: Who is like the operational manager.
vocab.tip: Manage names the action, manager the person, and operational the area of responsibility. Operations manager is another common job-title form.
vocab.example: The operational manager coordinated the daily schedule.
vocab.example_cn: 运营经理协调了日常安排。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Preserves source's operational manager rather than silently changing it to the more common operations manager.

vocab.definition: to supervise and take responsibility for an activity
vocab.source_excerpt: They oversee the building upkeep.
vocab.tip: over + see suggests watching over an activity. Distinguish oversee, supervise, from overlook, fail to notice.
vocab.example: She oversees the building's maintenance.
vocab.example_cn: 她负责监管这栋楼的维护工作。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Supervisory role, not simply seeing the building from above.

vocab.definition: paid a regular salary for work
vocab.source_excerpt: This is somebody who is salaried, who lives inside the house,
vocab.tip: salary changes y to -ied in salaried. Attach the word to regular pay, not a guarantee of a particular salary amount.
vocab.example: The organization hired a salaried administrator.
vocab.example_cn: 该组织聘请了一名领取固定薪水的行政人员。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Paid employee contrasted with undergraduate peer; no actual employment contract verified.

vocab.definition: small servings of strong alcoholic drink
vocab.source_excerpt: She's at the Tri Delta sorority house with her sorority sisters and they're just doing shots of vodka.
vocab.tip: Shot has several meanings; shots of vodka anchors the small-drink sense, not gunfire or photographs. The plural ends /ts/.
vocab.example: The menu listed shots of several spirits.
vocab.example_cn: 菜单列出了几种按小杯供应的烈酒。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Reported drinking quantity; does not define a universal serving volume or encourage consumption.

vocab.definition: a university student studying toward a first degree
vocab.source_excerpt: This is another undergraduate student who's also just trying to figure out college.
vocab.tip: Undergraduate is before completing a first degree; graduate can describe someone who has completed one. Here -ate has a reduced ending, not the verb sound /eɪt/.
vocab.example: The program is open to undergraduate students.
vocab.example_cn: 这个项目面向本科生开放。
vocab.context_review_note: Peer-student role contrasted with house director, not a description of the staff member.

vocab.definition: work or expense needed to keep something in good condition
vocab.source_excerpt: They oversee the building upkeep.
vocab.tip: Keep up something's condition becomes the noun upkeep. Picture recurring cleaning and repairs, not a one-time construction project.
vocab.example: The fees help pay for the building's upkeep.
vocab.example_cn: 这些费用用于分担建筑维护开支。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Facility maintenance under staff supervision.

vocab.definition: a strong, usually clear distilled alcoholic drink
vocab.source_excerpt: She's at the Tri Delta sorority house with her sorority sisters and they're just doing shots of vodka.
vocab.tip: Remember VOD-ka in two syllables with stress first. Keep the /dk/ consonants together and use vodka as a drink name, not a countable glass.
vocab.example: The report mentioned a bottle of vodka.
vocab.example_cn: 报告提到了一瓶伏特加。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Specific spirit named in allegations; later beer comparison is narrator speculation, not equivalent drink quantities.

vocab.definition: a person employed to control entry and keep order at a bar or club
vocab.cn: 酒吧或夜店门口的保安
vocab.source_excerpt: Now, Mooney's is also a defendant in this civil lawsuit where the bouncer and I'm assuming they asked for her ID.
vocab.tip: bounce + -er names a person in this informal job title. Picture the entry-control role rather than a person physically bouncing.
vocab.example: The bouncer checked the guests' IDs.
vocab.example_cn: 门口保安检查了来宾的证件。
vocab.context_review_note: The speaker assumes an ID check; that assumption is not converted into a verified original quote.

vocab.definition: a person responsible for looking after people, a building, or property
vocab.source_excerpt: Supposed to kind of be a caretaker.
vocab.tip: care + taker is someone who takes care of something. Here the role includes a residence and its occupants, not necessarily medical care.
vocab.example: The resident caretaker reported the broken door.
vocab.example_cn: 驻楼管理员报告了损坏的门。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Role description in narration, not proof of a legally defined duty in this case.

vocab.definition: a person who prepares and serves drinks at a bar
vocab.cn: 酒吧调酒师；吧台服务员
vocab.source_excerpt: The x's on her hands are to indicate to bartenders that jane doe is not of drinking age she's 20
vocab.tip: bar + tender: tend means look after or serve. A bartender tends the bar, not the door like a bouncer.
vocab.example: The bartender offered the guest a soft drink.
vocab.example_cn: 吧台服务员给这位客人提供了一杯软饮料。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Drink-service staff are the intended readers of the hand marks in the account.

vocab.definition: a business or public place such as a bar, restaurant, or hotel
vocab.source_excerpt: However the lawsuit alleges that mooney's is serving her drinks alcoholic beverages and there's like a whole there's a bunch of sorority sisters at this event at mooney's and they're all drinking despite the fact that she's under age at this establishment and
vocab.tip: establish + -ment can mean the act of founding or the place founded. Here at this establishment points to the bar, not the political establishment.
vocab.example: The establishment closes at midnight.
vocab.example_cn: 这家营业场所午夜关门。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Place/business sense; allegations about service remain attributed to the lawsuit.

vocab.definition: a fellow member of a college fraternity
vocab.source_excerpt: He's a fraternity brother at Chi Phi, and they have this huge, big fraternity house on campus at Cornell, the Chi Phi house, and she starts walking to the house.
vocab.tip: Brother is organizational kinship here, not a biological sibling. Combine it with fraternity to specify shared membership.
vocab.example: He met a fraternity brother at the reunion.
vocab.example_cn: 他在聚会上见到了一位同会成员。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Shared organization, not family relationship or proof of involvement in an allegation.

vocab.definition: different or not joined to something else
vocab.source_excerpt: Then around 10 p.m., Jane Doe and a few of her sorority sisters, they walk over to a separate bar called Lot 10.
vocab.tip: The adjective separate ends /rət/; the verb separate ends /reɪt/. Remember the middle spelling -para-, not -pera-.
vocab.example: The meeting will be held in a separate room.
vocab.example_cn: 会议将在另一间房间举行。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Adjective in a separate bar; distinguish venues instead of merging allegations about them.

vocab.definition: younger than twenty-one years old
vocab.source_excerpt: She's given another under 21 wristband, and it would appear at least from the filing that they do not serve her any alcoholic beverages here.

collocations.meaning_zh: 未满二十一岁标识腕带

vocab.tip: Under before a number means below that limit. Under 21 excludes exactly 21; use a hyphen when it modifies wristband.
vocab.example: Guests under 21 received a different wristband.
vocab.example_cn: 未满二十一岁的宾客领到了不同的腕带。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Age label in the account, not a statement about all legal rules in every jurisdiction.

vocab.definition: a band worn around the wrist, often for identification or entry
vocab.source_excerpt: She's given another under 21 wristband, and it would appear at least from the filing that they do not serve her any alcoholic beverages here.
vocab.tip: wrist + band names where the band goes. The w in wrist is silent; contrast wristband with waistband at the waist.
vocab.example: Each visitor received an identification wristband.
vocab.example_cn: 每位访客都领到了一条身份识别腕带。
vocab.ipa_source: freedictionaryapi.com (Wiktionary-derived)
vocab.context_review_note: Age/status marker, not by itself evidence that drinks were served.

vocab.definition: in an uncomfortable or socially uneasy way
vocab.source_excerpt: And I guess they're just like awkwardly sitting on the couch.
vocab.tip: awkward + -ly describes how an action feels or happens. Pair awkwardly sitting with an uncomfortable silence, not necessarily physical clumsiness.
vocab.example: They smiled awkwardly after the misunderstanding.
vocab.example_cn: 误会发生后，他们尴尬地笑了笑。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Narrator's impression of the seating interaction, introduced by I guess.

vocab.definition: a long upholstered seat for more than one person
vocab.source_excerpt: And I guess they're just like awkwardly sitting on the couch.
vocab.tip: Couch rhymes with ouch, not coach. Picture several people sitting on one long seat.
vocab.example: We sat on the couch and talked.
vocab.example_cn: 我们坐在沙发上聊天。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Furniture noun; not the verb couch a statement in particular terms.

vocab.definition: moving the body rhythmically, usually to music
vocab.source_excerpt: He hands her a beer, and there's some sort of dancing going on.
vocab.tip: dance drops final e before -ing: dancing. Keep the /s/ sound from dance; it does not become /k/.
vocab.example: They started dancing when the music began.
vocab.example_cn: 音乐响起时，他们开始跳舞。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Reported activity; dancing does not imply consent to later sexual acts.

vocab.definition: made a proposal to someone, especially a sexual invitation
vocab.source_excerpt: Matthew pulls Jane off to the side and she says, according to the lawsuit, he propositioned her, asks her if she wants to have a threesome with another one of his fraternity brothers.
vocab.tip: Proposition is a proposal; proposition someone is often a sexual proposition, unlike propose a work plan. Add -ed without another syllable after /n/.
vocab.example: She reported that a stranger had propositioned her.
vocab.example_cn: 她报告称，一个陌生人向她提出了性邀约。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: The source attributes the proposition to her lawsuit; the verb itself does not establish consent or coercion.

vocab.definition: not known, certain, or easy to understand
vocab.source_excerpt: But after dancing for what has been described by Matthew as three to five minutes – it's unclear how long it really was –
vocab.tip: un- negates clear. Separate unclear evidence from something disproved: unclear means not established either way.
vocab.example: It remains unclear how long the delay will last.
vocab.example_cn: 延误会持续多久仍不清楚。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Actual dancing duration is expressly uncertain despite one person's estimate.

vocab.definition: a room named for former students or members; here, the fraternity's own room label
vocab.cn: 校友室（此处为兄弟会房间名称）
vocab.source_excerpt: They're in what's called by the fraternity, the alumni room.
vocab.tip: Alumni are former students; alumni room is a room label, not proof that only alumni use it. Remember label and actual use can differ.
vocab.example: The tour included a room called the alumni room.
vocab.example_cn: 参观行程包括了一间名为校友室的房间。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Source describes mixed bedroom/social use; not a standardized room type with guaranteed access rules.

vocab.definition: to gather together in a group
vocab.source_excerpt: It's an unlocked space where people congregate.
vocab.tip: Connect congregate with congregation, a gathered group. The verb ends /ɡeɪt/ and pictures many people coming together.
vocab.example: Students often congregate in the courtyard.
vocab.example_cn: 学生们经常聚集在庭院里。
vocab.context_review_note: Gathering place, not a claim that every member was present.

vocab.definition: having a high alcohol concentration
vocab.source_excerpt: The lawsuit says during this time, defendant Matthew and Jonathan also plied plaintiff with marijuana and quote, Jamaican liquor believed to be some high proof rum.
vocab.tip: Proof here measures alcoholic strength, not evidence. Hyphenate high-proof when it comes before the drink name.
vocab.example: The article referred to high-proof spirits.
vocab.example_cn: 文章提到了高度烈酒。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Believed to be qualifies identification; no exact concentration inferred.

vocab.definition: cannabis used as a drug
vocab.source_excerpt: The lawsuit says during this time, defendant Matthew and Jonathan also plied plaintiff with marijuana and quote, Jamaican liquor believed to be some high proof rum.
vocab.tip: Remember marijuana with the /wɑ/ sound in the stressed syllable; the written j does not sound like the j in job.
vocab.example: The report mentioned alleged marijuana use.
vocab.example_cn: 报告提到了据称存在的大麻使用。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Substance name in a pleading; no use guidance or diagnosis.

vocab.definition: the person or organization bringing a civil lawsuit
vocab.source_excerpt: The lawsuit says during this time, defendant Matthew and Jonathan also plied plaintiff with marijuana and quote, Jamaican liquor believed to be some high proof rum.
vocab.tip: Connect plaintiff with complaint and contrast it with defendant. Keep double f and remember that a legal role is not a finding of truth.
vocab.example: The plaintiff submitted a written statement.
vocab.example_cn: 原告提交了一份书面陈述。
vocab.context_review_note: Role of the complainant in quoted legal wording, not interchangeable with prosecutor.

vocab.definition: like powder or consisting of fine dry particles
vocab.source_excerpt: According to the lawsuit, it seems Matthew is plopped up on the couch with Jonathan and they start passing around this plastic bag containing a white powdery substance, which Jane says they said was ketamine.
vocab.tip: powder + -y gives powdery. The adjective describes appearance or texture and does not identify the chemical substance.
vocab.example: A powdery layer covered the shelf.
vocab.example_cn: 架子上覆着一层粉末状的东西。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: White powder appearance is separate from the attributed claim that it was ketamine.

vocab.definition: trying to make someone do something through persistent influence or demands
vocab.source_excerpt: They start pressuring Jane into snorting ketamine with them.
vocab.tip: pressure drops final e before -ing. Learn pressure someone into + -ing, with the person between verb and into.
vocab.example: They were accused of pressuring staff into working late.
vocab.example_cn: 他们被指责向员工施压，要求员工加班。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Pressure allegation remains attributed; teaching example transfers structure to a work setting.

vocab.definition: drawing a powdered substance into the nose; also making a sharp nasal sound in other contexts
vocab.source_excerpt: They start pressuring Jane into snorting ketamine with them.

collocations.meaning_zh: 有关经鼻吸入毒品的指称

vocab.tip: Snort can be a sharp nose sound; in this context it describes intake through the nose. Keep -ing attached to snort without changing the base.
vocab.example: The report included allegations of snorting a substance.
vocab.example_cn: 报告包含有关经鼻吸入某种物质的指称。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Receptive vocabulary only; no technique or dosage is supplied.

vocab.definition: a type of physical material
vocab.source_excerpt: According to the lawsuit, it seems Matthew is plopped up on the couch with Jonathan and they start passing around this plastic bag containing a white powdery substance, which Jane says they said was ketamine.
vocab.tip: Substance can mean material or meaningful content. A bag containing a substance anchors the material sense, without guessing its identity.
vocab.example: The container held an unknown substance.
vocab.example_cn: 容器里装着一种不明物质。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Identification is nested attribution: Jane says they said it was ketamine, not a confirmed laboratory finding.

vocab.definition: not secured by a lock
vocab.source_excerpt: It's an unlocked space where people congregate.

collocations.meaning_zh: 让房间保持未上锁状态

vocab.tip: un- reverses locked. Locked and unlocked both end /kt/; add no extra vowel after k.
vocab.example: The side door was left unlocked.
vocab.example_cn: 侧门没有上锁。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Physical access state, not proof that the room was open to everyone with permission.

vocab.definition: the state of the penis becoming firm and enlarged
vocab.source_excerpt: But at some point the lawsuit states that Matthew could no longer maintain an erection.
vocab.tip: Erect can mean upright; erection names a resulting state. Context determines the anatomical sense rather than construction of a building.
vocab.example: The clinical report mentioned difficulty maintaining an erection.
vocab.example_cn: 临床报告提到了难以维持勃起的情况。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Anatomical term in an attributed assault account; teaching example is clinical, not erotic or diagnostic.

vocab.definition: during the same period of time
vocab.source_excerpt: Meanwhile, Jonathan keeps, according to the lawsuit, keeps trying to reach for her private parts down there.
vocab.tip: meanwhile links simultaneous timelines. While already signals time; meanwhile introduces what another person is doing during that period.
vocab.example: I prepared the slides. Meanwhile, my colleague checked the figures.
vocab.example_cn: 我准备幻灯片。与此同时，同事核对了数据。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Signals concurrent actions, not permission or causal connection.

vocab.definition: a message sent to several people in a shared conversation
vocab.source_excerpt: And Jonathan, the one that Matthew wanted to have a threesome with, allegedly, right, sends a group message to the…
vocab.tip: Group identifies the audience; message is the communication. A group message can reach many recipients without proving each read it.
vocab.example: She sent a group message about the meeting.
vocab.example_cn: 她发送了一条有关会议的群消息。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Source alleges a message to a chapter chat; recipients are not automatically participants in the events.

vocab.definition: the name of a social messaging application
vocab.source_excerpt: Xi chapter Snapchat.
vocab.tip: The brand combines snap, a quick picture, and chat, conversation. Preserve its capital S as a proper name.
vocab.example: The report referred to a Snapchat group.
vocab.example_cn: 报告提到了一个 Snapchat 群组。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Brand/platform identification only; no assumptions about current features or message persistence.

vocab.definition: making something clearer or easier to understand
vocab.cn: 澄清含义的；帮助弄清楚的
vocab.source_excerpt: And surely one of them must ask clarifying questions.
vocab.tip: Clear and clarify belong to the same meaning family. Clarify keeps y before -ing: clarifying questions clear up uncertainty.
vocab.example: She asked a clarifying question about the deadline.
vocab.example_cn: 她问了一个问题，以弄清截止日期。
vocab.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (ARPABET converted to broad IPA)
vocab.context_review_note: Questions intended to establish what the message means, not confirmation that anyone actually asked them.

vocab.definition: agreed to freely by the people involved
vocab.cn: 双方或各方自愿同意的
vocab.source_excerpt: Maybe if you engaged in some sexual activity that was consensual and you texted some like, oh, I did some crazy stuff and said a derogatory name.
vocab.tip: Consent is the base idea in consensual; the adjective describes mutual agreement. Do not confuse consent with merely being present.
vocab.example: They described their relationship as consensual.
